physical_harm: Victim was shot in the head, chest and various parts of his body, resulting in death
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the testimonies of the eye-witnesses and the Test Identification Parade (TIP) as part of the evidence, but noted that the TIP was not conducted properly and was delayed.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as suffering from various infirmities, contradictions, and inconsistencies in their testimonies, making their credibility questionable.
procedural_irregularity: Test Identification Parade (TIP) was not conducted properly and was delayed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the trial court's conviction was well reasoned and well considered, and that the evidence of eye-witnesses and the Test Identification Parade (TIP) conclusively established that Al and Al 2 had fired on the deceased, with the recovery of the weapon and ballistic report further strengthening the case.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the eye-witness testimonies suffered various infirmities, contradictions, and the TIP was not conducted properly and was delayed, thus the High Court rightly granted the benefit of doubt to the accused as their identity was not clearly established by the prosecution.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that when an attack is made on the injured/deceased by a mob in a crowded place and the eyewitnesses had little time to see the accused, the substantive evidence should be sufficiently corroborated by a test identification parade held soon after the occurrence, and any delay in holding the test identification parade may be fatal to the prosecution case.
precedent_relied_upon: Siddanki Ram Reddy v. State of Andhra Pradesh (2010) 7 SCC 697
